planning.goal: Run the existing DemoQA regression suite reproducibly in Docker and publish traceable test evidence from Jenkins.
sequence: Create the Epic and confirm the project supports Epic, Story, and Task issue types.
Create the Stories and Tasks using the payloads below.
Add created child issue keys to the Epic through the Jira Agile REST API.
Create or select a two-week sprint on the SCRUM board; add the Stories and Tasks after confirming team capacity.
planning.estimationGuidance: Estimate during refinement using the team's scale; do not assume project-specific story-point fields or sprint IDs.

jql.demoqaBacklog: project = SCRUM AND labels = demoqa AND statusCategory != Done ORDER BY Rank ASC
jql.epicChildren: project = SCRUM AND parent = "<EPIC_KEY>" ORDER BY Rank ASC
jql.unassignedToSprint: project = SCRUM AND labels = demoqa AND sprint is EMPTY ORDER BY priority DESC

fields.summary: DemoQA automated regression and CI delivery

content.text: Deliver a reliable, traceable Playwright regression workflow for https://demoqa.com/ using Docker and Jenkins.
Epic acceptance criteria:
The existing Playwright suite runs in a reproducible browser-matched Docker image.
Jenkins checks out the GitHub repository, builds the image, executes tests, and publishes JUnit and HTML reports.
Test cases retain stable IDs and Jira links; secrets are stored only in approved credential stores.

children.summary: Run DemoQA Playwright regression tests in Docker
children.description:
As a QA engineer, I want the existing Playwright suite in a version-matched container so that local and CI results use the same browser runtime.

Acceptance criteria:
- Docker image installs dependencies with npm ci and uses the matching Playwright browser image.
- The full suite runs headlessly with one worker and returns a failing exit code if any test fails.
- JUnit XML and the Playwright HTML report are written to mounted output directories.
- Build and run commands are documented and verified on a Docker host.

children.summary: Run Dockerized DemoQA regression on GitHub changes in Jenkins
children.description:
As a developer, I want Jenkins to run the Dockerized regression suite for repository changes so that failures and reports are visible without manual execution.

Acceptance criteria:
- Jenkins checks out the configured GitHub branch and builds the test image.
- A GitHub webhook or SCM polling triggers the pipeline after changes.
- Test failures mark the build failed; successful runs publish JUnit results.
- HTML reports, test results, and useful failure evidence are archived.
- Jenkins uses managed credentials and an agent with Docker access.

children.summary: Maintain DemoQA test case and Jira traceability
children.description:
As a QA engineer, I want stable test case IDs and Jira links maintained with the automation so that coverage, execution, and backlog work remain traceable.

Acceptance criteria:
- Test case JSON and CSV stay synchronized.
- Automated tests include the local case ID and corresponding Jira key when available.
- Jira issues include scenario, steps, expected result, priority, and labels.
- Existing valid Jira issues are reused; duplicate issues are not created.
